```{r a5-setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6.5,
  fig.height = 5.8, dpi = 120, out.width = "100%")
options(width = 82)
```

`postrank` does not fit statistical models. You fit your model outside the
package (for example in Stan, brms, or JAGS) and supply posterior draws, a
conditional normal or mixture distribution, or comparison probabilities that
you have already computed. Your results depend on the posterior you supply,
and any dependence across entities or criteria that was dropped before export
cannot be recovered inside `postrank`.

This article builds a one-criterion draw input, extends it to two criteria,
computes analytic comparison probabilities from a normal law, and imports an
external probability matrix. All examples run without an optimization solver.
In an empirical study, replace the synthetic draw generator below with output
from your fitted model and describe that model and its sampling history.

## Targets and draw array layout {#decide-what-one-row-of-your-export-means}

Entity IDs identify the same sites, schools, employers, or areas throughout an
analysis. Use character IDs so leading zeros (such as `"01001"`) are kept.
Criterion IDs name the target quantities being compared, along with their
units, time period, and priority direction. Larger values on the oriented
scale mean higher priority, and grade 1 is the highest-priority group.

Joint posterior draws are stored as a three-dimensional numeric array with
dimensions `draws x entities x criteria` (`S x n x K`), in which every draw
holds one value for every entity and every criterion from the same posterior
state. With a single criterion (`K = 1`), keep the third dimension as an
`S x n x 1` array rather than dropping it to a matrix.

| Posterior information you have | Constructor | What to preserve |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Joint posterior draws across entities and criteria | `postrank_draws()` | Entity and criterion axes, within-draw pairing, and sampling history (`"iid"` or `"mcmc"`) |
| Separate draw matrices for each criterion | `postrank_draws(..., metadata = ...)` | Joint entity vectors within each criterion and each fit's sampling history |
| Posterior draws from the `posterior` package | `postrank_draws()` (or `as_postrank_posterior()` for `draws_array`) | Variable mapping to `(entity_id, criterion_id)` and chain/iteration coordinates |
| Conditional normal posterior | `postrank_gaussian_coefficients()` | Means, covariance matrices, conditional-independence scope, and source metadata |
| Shared-state normal mixture | `postrank_mixture_coefficients()` | Shared hyperparameter states, weights, and conditional moments |
| Discrete finite posterior with exact rational weights | `as_postrank_draws()` | Complete joint states and integer numerators over a common denominator |
| Precomputed comparison probabilities | `postrank_probabilities()` | Event direction, source conditioning, zero-tie assumption, and any symmetry adjustment |

The last four constructors apply only when that normal law, mixture, finite
distribution, or probability table is part of your intended statistical
analysis; a table of marginal means and standard errors alone does not define
a joint posterior over entity pairs.

## Building a one-criterion draw input

`pr_tutorial$law` defines independent normal distributions for six fictional
sites (`A` through `F`) in illustrative standardized units. Below we simulate
`S = 512` independent joint draws for `score_A` from that synthetic law. With
real data, export the posterior draws of your target quantities directly at
full precision instead of simulating independent normal draws from marginal
summaries (unless independent normal posteriors are your actual model).

```{r a5-generate-one}
library(postrank)
law <- pr_tutorial$law
ids <- rownames(law$means)
S <- 512L
sd_A <- sqrt(law$covariance["score_A", "score_A", ])
set.seed(725)
values <- array(NA_real_, c(S, length(ids), 1L),
  dimnames = list(draw = NULL, entity = ids, criterion = "score_A"))
for (i in seq_along(ids)) {
  values[, i, 1] <- rnorm(S, law$means[i, "score_A"], sd_A[i])
}
dim(values)
```

For a numeric draw array, `postrank_draws()` requires a sampling `regime`
(`"iid"` for independent draws or `"mcmc"` for Markov chain draws) and eight
declaration blocks describing the draws and their source. `postrank_describe()`
collects these descriptions as plain arguments. It rejects generic placeholders
such as `"TBD"`, `"unknown"`, and `"none"` in scientific descriptions and in the
shared `label`. Criterion names and `data_version` must be nonempty
identifiers. For example, `data_version = "none"` can record a simulation
with no versioned source data.

```{r a5-declarations}
declarations <- postrank_describe(
  estimand = c(score_A = "Site-level latent score A in the specified Gaussian law"),
  population = "Six fictional sites A through F",
  time = "Static tutorial scenario; no observed time period",
  units = law$units,
  data = "No observations; means and variances fixed by pr_tutorial$law",
  model = "Independent normal site scores with the supplied means and variances",
  identification = "Each target is a directly specified coordinate of the fixed law.",
  joint = "Each draw holds all six sites from one independent state of the score_A law.",
  sampling = "512 independent draws from rnorm() after set.seed(725); no warmup or thinning.",
  ties = "Independent continuous normal scores have positive variances, so exact equality has probability zero.",
  software = "Base R rnorm()",
  source = "Array values generated from pr_tutorial$law in this article",
  label = "a5-iid-score-A",
  data_version = "1",
  values = values
)
draws <- postrank_draws(values, regime = "iid", declarations = declarations)
draws$entity_ids
draws$criterion_ids
```

Every scientific description in `postrank_describe()` is written by you; the
helper fills in only the repeated identifier fields (from `label`) and the
array format string (from `values`), and `population`, `time`, and `units`
accept either one shared string or a character vector named by criterion. In a
hierarchical model where entities share random effects or hyperparameters, keep
all entities paired within each posterior draw: shuffling draws separately by
entity preserves marginal intervals while changing the pairwise comparison
probabilities.

By default (`orientation = "higher"` in `postrank_draws()`), larger raw values
mean higher priority. When smaller raw values mean higher priority (for
example, chronic absence or incarceration rates), pass the raw draws to
`postrank_draws()` and supply a full or partial criterion-named vector of
`"higher"` and `"lower"`, such as `orientation = c(rate = "lower")` (`orientation`
is an argument of `postrank_draws()`, not `postrank_describe()`, and any omitted
criterion defaults to `"higher"`). That negates `"lower"` criteria once and
records the sign flip in `targets`; do not negate the raw draws beforehand as
well, or you will flip the sign twice. Downstream report-card means and
intervals stay on that negated scale, so negating them back to raw rates swaps
`lower_<criterion>` and `upper_<criterion>`; see
[Grading California schools on chronic absence](a2-cde-accountability.html)
for an example.

### Pairwise comparison probabilities {#inspect-the-comparisons-before-choosing-grades}

```{r a5-aggregate-one}
pairwise <- postrank_pairwise(draws)
round(pairwise$e[, , "score_A"], 3)
```

Entry `e[i, j, k]` estimates $\Pr(\theta_{ik} \le \theta_{jk})$, the posterior
expected error if the report places entity `i` in a higher-priority grade than
entity `j` on criterion `k`. Diagonal entries are `NA` because an entity is
not compared with itself. An estimated `0` off the diagonal means that
$\theta_i \le \theta_j$ did not occur among the `512` draws; it does not prove
that the true probability under the continuous law is zero.

When subsetting a multi-criterion draw array down to one criterion, use
`drop = FALSE` (`larger_array[, , "score_A", drop = FALSE]`) so the third
dimension stays intact. Keep the draws at full precision. Rounding can create
exact ties between entities, and `postrank_draws()` stops on exact ties;
adding random noise to break them would change the posterior you described.
For posteriors in which exact ties are real, see `?as_postrank_tie_draws`.

## Multiple criteria, separate criterion fits, and MCMC history

Next we add `score_B` while keeping the exact same `score_A` draws. In
`pr_tutorial$law`, the two criteria are independent within each site; in a
joint model fitted to real data, export both criteria from the same posterior
draws so any cross-criterion dependence is preserved.

```{r a5-two-sim}
two_values <- array(NA_real_, c(S, length(ids), 2L),
  dimnames = list(draw = NULL, entity = ids, criterion = colnames(law$means)))
two_values[, , "score_A"] <- values[, , "score_A"]
for (i in seq_along(ids)) {
  two_values[, i, "score_B"] <- rnorm(S, law$means[i, "score_B"],
    sqrt(law$covariance["score_B", "score_B", i]))
}
```

Next we describe both criteria and build the two-criterion `postrank_draws`
object, confirming that `score_A`'s pairwise comparison probabilities are
unchanged:

```{r a5-two-criteria}
two_decl <- postrank_describe(
  estimand = c(
    score_A = "Site-level latent score A",
    score_B = "Site-level latent score B"
  ),
  population = "Six fictional sites A through F",
  time = "Static tutorial scenario; no observed time period",
  units = c(score_A = law$units, score_B = law$units),
  data = "No observations; means and variances fixed by pr_tutorial$law",
  model = "Independent normal site scores across sites and criteria",
  identification = "Each target is a directly specified coordinate of the fixed law.",
  joint = "Each draw holds all six sites and both criteria from one independent state.",
  sampling = "512 independent draws from rnorm(); score_A uses set.seed(725).",
  ties = "Independent continuous normal scores have positive variances, so exact equality has probability zero.",
  software = "Base R rnorm()",
  source = "Array two_values generated from pr_tutorial$law in this article",
  label = "a5-iid-score-A-and-B",
  data_version = "1",
  values = two_values
)
two_draws <- postrank_draws(two_values, regime = "iid", declarations = two_decl)
two_pairwise <- postrank_pairwise(two_draws)
identical(pairwise$e[, , "score_A"], two_pairwise$e[, , "score_A"])
```

When different criteria come from separate model fits, row `s` in fit 1 and
row `s` in fit 2 do not represent a shared posterior state. Pass those draws
as a named list of `S_k x n` matrices (one matrix per criterion, with every
entity paired within each row and possibly different draw counts `S_k`) via
`postrank_draws(matrices, metadata = criterion_metadata)`; see
`?postrank_draws` for the metadata fields. Separate criterion matrices
support criterion-weighted expected loss, because that loss adds expected
errors criterion by criterion, whereas probabilities for composite linear
combinations or simultaneous dominance across criteria remain unavailable:

```{r criterionwise-sketch, eval = FALSE}
# m1, m2: separate S_k x n draw matrices with matching entity column names;
# metadata: list describing targets, context, provenance, and per-criterion
# sampling history without cross-criterion pairing (see ?postrank_draws).
draws_cw <- postrank_draws(list(need1 = m1, need2 = m2), metadata = metadata)
```

For Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) output, record the original chain layout.
With a 3D `S x n x K` array in which the
chains' post-warmup iterations are stacked contiguously chain by chain (rows
`1:m` for chain 1, `(m + 1):(2 * m)` for chain 2, and so on), pass
`regime = "mcmc"` together with integer `chains` (the number of chains),
`warmup_per_chain` (iterations discarded per chain before export), and `thin`
(`1L` when unthinned). The bundled `pr_toy_mcmc` contains four stationary
two-state Markov chains of 512 iterations each. The generator retained every
iteration, including the first. Within each state, the three sites have
distinct targets on each criterion, so the model gives zero probability to a
between-site tie.

```{r a5-mcmc-example}
mcmc_draws <- postrank_draws(
  pr_toy_mcmc, regime = "mcmc",
  chains = 4L, warmup_per_chain = 0L, thin = 1L,
  declarations = attr(pr_toy_mcmc, "law")[["declarations"]]
)
chain_history <- mcmc_draws$joint_draws$sampling$chain_history
do.call(rbind, lapply(chain_history, function(h) {
  data.frame(chain = h$chain_id, retained = length(h$retained_iterations),
    warmup_removed = length(h$warmup_iterations),
    thin = unique(diff(h$retained_iterations)))
}))
```

If your draws are already in a `posterior` package object (`draws_array`,
`draws_df`, or `draws_matrix` from `cmdstanr` or `brms`), pass them to
`postrank_draws()` with `variables`, `metadata`, and `source_coordinates` for
every retained draw (or pass a `posterior::draws_array` directly to
`as_postrank_posterior()` with `variable_map`, `metadata`, and
`source_coordinates`). Using the installed synthetic generator, we can package
`postrank_toy`'s 32 draws as a one-chain `posterior::draws_array` and verify
that mapping them back recovers the identical `input_identity`:

```{r a5-posterior-route}
if (requireNamespace("posterior", quietly = TRUE)) {
  source(system.file("examples", "make-synthetic-input.R",
    package = "postrank", mustWork = TRUE))
  meta <- make_postrank_synthetic_input()
  vals <- meta[["joint_draws"]][["tensor"]][["values"]]
  map <- meta[["joint_draws"]][["variable_map"]]
  vars <- vapply(map, `[[`, "", "source_target_variable_id")
  src <- array(NA_real_, c(dim(vals)[1], 1L, length(vars)),
    dimnames = list(iteration = NULL, chain = "1", variable = vars))
  for (m in seq_along(map)) {
    src[, 1, vars[m]] <- vals[, map[[m]][["entity_id"]], map[[m]][["criterion_id"]]]
  }
  coords <- lapply(seq_len(dim(vals)[1]), function(s) {
    list(slot_id = dimnames(vals)[["draw"]][[s]], iteration_index = s, chain_index = 1L)
  })
  meta[["joint_draws"]][["tensor"]][["values"]] <- NULL
  from_posterior <- postrank_draws(posterior::as_draws_array(src),
    variables = map, metadata = meta, source_coordinates = coords)
  identical(from_posterior[["validation"]][["input_identity"]],
    postrank_toy[["validation"]][["input_identity"]])
}
```

## Analytic probabilities from a normal or mixture posterior {#a-gaussian-law-can-supply-probabilities-directly}

When your conditional posterior is normal, `postrank_gaussian_coefficients()`
computes the pairwise directional-error probabilities analytically without
Monte Carlo simulation. Below we evaluate the same `score_A` normal law
analytically and compare three site pairs against the 512-draw Monte Carlo
estimates:

```{r a5-analytic}
analytic <- postrank_gaussian_coefficients(
  means = law$means[, "score_A", drop = FALSE],
  covariance = law$covariance["score_A", "score_A", , drop = FALSE],
  conditional_independence = "entities_given_shared_h",
  provenance = pr_tutorial$one$provenance
)
selected_pairs <- rbind(c(1L, 2L), c(3L, 4L), c(5L, 6L))
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  row = ids[selected_pairs[, 1]], column = ids[selected_pairs[, 2]],
  draw_estimate = pairwise$e[, , 1][selected_pairs],
  analytic = analytic$e[, , 1][selected_pairs]
), digits = 4, row.names = FALSE)
```

Both columns target the same normal law: `draw_estimate` has Monte Carlo
variation across the `512` simulated draws, while `analytic` evaluates the
normal cumulative distribution function of each pairwise score difference.
`postrank_gaussian_coefficients()` requires named entity and criterion axes,
symmetric positive-definite covariance matrices, a stated
`conditional_independence` scope, and `provenance` metadata recording where
the moments came from.

In a hierarchical model where entities are conditionally normal given shared
hyperparameters, `postrank_mixture_coefficients()` averages those conditional
Gaussian probabilities across hyperparameter states (with fixed mixture
weights or hyperparameter MCMC metadata), preserving the cross-entity
dependence induced by the shared hyperparameters. For discrete posteriors
defined on a finite list of joint states with exact rational probabilities,
`as_postrank_draws()` stores integer mass numerators over a common
denominator (and `postrank_pairwise()` can keep exact rational probabilities
when the optional `gmp` package is installed).

## Importing precomputed comparison probabilities {#import-probabilities-without-inventing-a-posterior-sample}

When an external numerical integration routine computes pairwise comparison
probabilities directly, pass them to `postrank_probabilities()` as a named
square matrix (one criterion) or an `entity x entity x criterion` array,
together with `event` (`"directional_error"` when entry `[i, j]` is
$\Pr(\theta_i \le \theta_j)$, or `"higher_priority"` when entry `[i, j]` is
$\Pr(\theta_i > \theta_j)$). Here we package the analytic `score_A`
probabilities together with matching 90% marginal intervals:

```{r a5-probability-input}
means <- law$means[, "score_A", drop = FALSE]
level <- 0.90
half_width <- qnorm((1 + level) / 2) * sd_A
probability_input <- postrank_probabilities(
  analytic$e[, , "score_A"], criterion = "score_A",
  event = "directional_error", zero_ties = TRUE, margin = 0,
  source = list(
    kind = "analytic_reference",
    description = "Normal-CDF comparisons for independent site scores in pr_tutorial$law",
    conditioning = law$conditioning
  ),
  targets = c(score_A = "Illustrative standardized site score A; larger is higher priority"),
  summaries = list(
    means = means, same_targets = TRUE,
    description = "Means and central equal-tail intervals from the same fixed normal site laws",
    lower = sweep(means, 1, half_width, "-"),
    upper = sweep(means, 1, half_width, "+"), level = level
  )
)
probability_input$correction$method
```

Row and column entity IDs must match in the same order, diagonal entries must
be `NA`, off-diagonal entries must lie in `[0, 1]`, and opposite directions
must sum to `1` within tolerance (`zero_ties = TRUE` and `margin = 0`). If
numerical quadrature leaves tiny reverse-sum discrepancies, set
`correction = "symmetric"` with an explicit `tolerance`; the object records
the raw probabilities and the largest adjustment made, which measures only
that symmetrization step rather than quadrature or model error.

```{r a5-probability-map, fig.cap="Directional-error probabilities Pr(theta_i <= theta_j) for Score A across the six sites. Gray diagonal cells mark self-comparisons (NA).", fig.alt="Six-by-six heatmap of directional-error probabilities for sites A through F on Score A, with gray diagonal cells."}
postrank_plot_pairwise(probability_input, max_entities = NULL)
```

Optional `summaries` supply the posterior means and equal-tail intervals used
on report cards and must describe the same oriented targets and units as the
comparison probabilities. Because only the endpoints at `level = 0.90` are
stored here, other interval levels cannot be computed from `probability_input`,
and draw-based Monte Carlo diagnostics are unavailable. See
[Grading large employers on race and gender contact gaps](a3-krw-race-gender.html)
for an empirical-Bayes case study built with `postrank_probabilities()`.

## Reading and writing JSON draw files {#json-draw-files-and-synthetic-example}

To exchange posterior draws across languages or archive them with their
descriptions, use `write_postrank_draws()` and `read_postrank_draws()`.
The JSON file stores `schema_version = "applied-0.1"`. The object in R keeps
that value in `input_schema_version` and uses `schema_version = "0.1.0"` for
its in-memory layout. The package ships a complete example file,
`examples/synthetic-iid.json`, holding the same
32-draw, three-entity (`"001"`, `"site-B"`, `"site C"`), two-criterion synthetic
normal sample as `postrank_toy`:

```{r load-example}
path <- system.file("examples", "synthetic-iid.json",
  package = "postrank", mustWork = TRUE)
toy_draws <- read_postrank_draws(path)
toy_draws[c("input_schema_version", "schema_version")]
toy_draws[["entity_ids"]]
toy_draws[["criterion_ids"]]
dim(toy_draws[["joint_draws"]][["tensor"]][["values"]])
```

The companion script `examples/make-synthetic-input.R` defines
`make_postrank_synthetic_input()` without running it on `source()` and restores
the caller's random-number state; regenerating the list and converting it with
`as_postrank_draws()` matches the stored sample within `1e-12` across platforms:

```{r inspect-generator}
generator <- system.file("examples", "make-synthetic-input.R",
  package = "postrank", mustWork = TRUE)
source(generator)
toy_spec <- make_postrank_synthetic_input()
rebuilt <- as_postrank_draws(toy_spec)
rebuilt_values <- rebuilt[["joint_draws"]][["tensor"]][["values"]]
stored_values <- toy_draws[["joint_draws"]][["tensor"]][["values"]]
max(abs(rebuilt_values - stored_values)) <= 1e-12
toy_spec[["targets"]][[1]][c("criterion_id", "estimand", "units")]
```

`write_postrank_draws()` formats numbers at 17-digit precision so reading
the file back reproduces the floating-point draw array identically, while
`read_postrank_draws()` rejects duplicate JSON keys, malformed numbers,
out-of-range integers, and invalid Unicode surrogates:

```{r roundtrip}
copy_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".json")
write_postrank_draws(toy_draws, copy_path)
roundtrip <- read_postrank_draws(copy_path)
identical(roundtrip[["joint_draws"]][["tensor"]][["values"]], stored_values)
unlink(copy_path)
```

## Input validation versus statistical model checking {#keep-validation-and-model-checking-separate}

Input validation checks object structure and that required descriptions are
present; it does not check whether your statistical model is appropriate,
whether targets are identified, or whether MCMC chains have converged. Omitting
any of the eight required blocks in `postrank_declarations()` stops with an
error, and we can inspect the validation flags returned by
`validate_postrank_draws()` directly:

```{r a5-validation}
tryCatch(
  postrank_declarations(targets = declarations[["targets"]],
    context = declarations[["context"]]),
  error = conditionMessage
)
validation <- validate_postrank_draws(draws)
validation[c("valid", "schema_checked", "source_values_checked",
             "jointness_verified", "convergence_verified")]
```

`valid` is `TRUE` because the array dimensions, axis names, finite values,
ties, and eight required descriptions passed the package's R checks.
`schema_checked` is `FALSE` because this route uses no external JSON Schema
validator. `source_values_checked` is `FALSE` because the example supplied an
array directly. When you import a `posterior` object, `as_postrank_posterior()`
compares mapped values with that source and records the result.
`jointness_verified` and `convergence_verified` remain `FALSE` on both routes.
Assessing dependence and convergence requires evidence from the fitted model
and its sampling run.

| Function or input | What it checks |
|:--|:--|
| `postrank_describe()` | Checks the description arguments and builds a bundle with `postrank_declarations()`. If it derives `format` from `values`, it checks for a three-dimensional numeric array and records its type and dimensions. |
| `postrank_declarations()` | Checks the eight required blocks and rejects generic placeholders in the descriptions. The full form treats `targets$criterion_id`, `context$data_version`, and `origin$fit_id` as nonempty identifiers exempt from the placeholder check. |
| Numeric-array `postrank_draws()` | Rechecks the declarations and validates the array axes, entity and criterion IDs, finite values, ties, and sampling layout. |
| `postrank_draws_from_array()` | Validates the required declaration fields, the draw array, and its sampling layout. The placeholder check applies only in the friendly constructors above. |
| `as_postrank_draws()` | Validates an in-memory input's required fields, coordinates, and numeric contents. |
| `read_postrank_draws()` | Parses the JSON file, checks JSON syntax and duplicate keys, then calls `as_postrank_draws()` on the decoded input. |
| `write_postrank_draws()` | Validates the supplied input with `as_postrank_draws()`, encodes it as JSON, and checks the encoded file structure before saving. |
| Criterion-wise matrix list `postrank_draws(list(...), metadata = ...)` | Matches each matrix to its criterion and validates its coordinates and sampling metadata. |
| `as_postrank_posterior()` | Checks the posterior object's draw coordinates and variable mappings, then compares each mapped numeric value with the source. |

Once an input (`draws`, `mcmc_draws`, `analytic`, or `probability_input`) is
ready, pass it to `postrank()` with your chosen policy settings and solver.
Gurobi is the default solver and requires a license; the call below
(`eval = FALSE`) selects the open-source HiGHS solver
(`install.packages("highs")`):

```{r a5-optional-solve, eval=FALSE}
result <- postrank(draws, weights = c(score_A = 1), tau = 0.25,
  G_max = 3L, backend = "highs", level = 0.90,
  control = postrank_control(time_limit = 30), fragility = FALSE)
```
